trigger: git reset --hard while new files exist only in the index (never committed)
consequence: the staged-only files are deleted and live in no commit, no stash, no reflog -- the work is gone without a trace
prevention: segment the commit chain, or stash first; never assume reset preserves what only the index holds

trigger: force-pushing a branch after review comments were already given on it
consequence: the PR loses its review context: comments anchor to lines and commits that no longer exist, approvals are invalidated, and the discussion history is orphaned
prevention: append a fixup commit and let reviewers re-review the delta; reserve force push for branches nobody has reviewed

trigger: committing task docs, agent memory logs, or machine-absolute paths to a PUBLIC repository
consequence: usernames, home-directory layout and internal plans leak into the public tree; secret_scan only recognizes key shapes, not content that belongs to the public face
prevention: run the privacy gate (scripts/privacy_scan.py, shrink-only ratchet) before pushing; keep local state under ignored paths

trigger: restore/cleanup logic that deletes 'extra' files directly (os.remove) inside a tool
consequence: deletion bypasses every ledger -- no entry, no reason, no way back; one wrong snapshot silently destroys newer work
prevention: route every deletion through the recycle bin (trash put_paths) and fail the restore when the bin refuses

trigger: parsing git diff with only '+++ b/<path>' as the file header
consequence: whole-file deletions print '+++ /dev/null' with no b/ line, so deleted files never enter the parser's table and every rule scoped to them silently skips
prevention: keep the '--- a/<path>' as pending and mark it deleted on '+++ /dev/null' (the L96 fix in tools/constraints.py)

trigger: writing Win32 Job Object class ids and LimitFlags from memory
consequence: a wrong class id reports 'invalid parameter' (87) and a wrong flag bit masquerades as a length error (24) -- the error text points at the wrong layer and the fix drifts
prevention: derive constants by scanning with an all-zero buffer for the accepted (class, size) pair and verify each flag bit separately; fail closed when the call refuses

trigger: adding an orchestration step without updating the expected-step-sequence assertion in the selftest
consequence: a never-green assertion sits in the suite looking like coverage -- expectation and implementation have drifted
prevention: derive the expected step list from the orchestration code's unconditional adds (skipped steps still appear) and change both sides in one commit

trigger: selftest fixtures referencing a machine-specific repo root, or files that an upstream refactor has deleted
consequence: assertions pass on one machine as an environment lottery and fail everywhere else, or reference files that no longer exist
prevention: derive every fixture path from the test's own location and assert against files verified to exist in the tree

trigger: asserting on Chinese output piped between processes on a Windows console
consequence: the writer encodes by locale (GBK) while the reader decodes by console codepage -- the same code is green in a UTF-8 console and pseudo-red in a GBK one
prevention: pin UTF-8 on both sides (console OutputEncoding plus PYTHONUTF8/PYTHONIOENCODING) and keep machine-readable receipts pure ASCII

trigger: committing shell scripts from Windows, where git does not record the exec bit
consequence: scripts land as 100644 and CI on linux fails with exit 126 Permission denied, far from the real cause
prevention: git update-index --chmod=+x the scripts (the permission bit is part of the script); assert executability from the index, cross-platform
